facts: Austin is the capital city of Texas and is known as the Live Music Capital of the World.
The Ann and Roy Butler Hike-and-Bike Trail circles Lady Bird Lake in the heart of downtown Austin.
Austin enjoys over 300 sunny days each year, making it a fantastic destination for outdoor runners.
Lady Bird Lake was created in 1960 as a cooling pond for a municipal power plant.
The iconic trail around Lady Bird Lake spans ten miles of continuous, scenic crushed limestone paths.
Austin's Congress Avenue Bridge hosts the largest urban bat colony in North America every summer.
Zilker Park sits along the trail and hosts the famous Austin City Limits Music Festival every autumn.
Barton Springs Pool is a natural spring-fed pool that maintains a refreshing sixty-eight degrees year-round.
Texas barbecue and breakfast tacos are famous local staples that runners love to enjoy post-workout.
The city was originally named Waterloo before being renamed in honor of Stephen F. Austin.
The Austin Marathon attracts thousands of runners from around the globe every February.
Deep Eddy Pool is the oldest swimming pool in Texas, fed by fresh spring water.
Over one million Mexican free-tailed bats emerge from under the Congress Avenue Bridge at sunset.
Austin is home to the flagship campus of the University of Texas, founded in 1883.
Lady Bird Johnson led beautification efforts that helped create the lush greenways surrounding the trail.
The Boardwalk section of the lake trail offers stunning views of the Austin skyline over the water.
Mount Bonnell provides one of the highest points in Austin, featuring breathtaking views of the Colorado River.
Austin features more than two hundred and fifty parks and green spaces throughout the metropolitan area.
Famous musician Willie Nelson moved to Austin in the 1970s, helping shape its iconic music scene.
The Texas State Capitol building in Austin is taller than the United States Capitol in Washington, D.C.
